research.abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Bacterial genomes encode a large repertoire of multidrug efflux pumps, which could theoretically combine to achieve exceptionally high levels of resistance. To delineate the extent of resistance achievable through efflux driven adaptation, we performed adaptive laboratory evolution of Mycobacterium smegmatis mc²155 wild-type and efflux-deleted (ΔlfrA, ΔefpA) strains against ethidium bromide, a broad-spectrum efflux substrate. Despite prolonged selection, resistance reproducibly plateaued at 8-16 fold increase in MIC under the tested conditions. This plateau emerged through distinct evolutionary trajectories characterized by non-overlapping efflux pump sets: from overexpression of the well-characterized lfrA to upregulation of multiple uncharacterized pumps, all conferring cross-resistance. Genetic reconstruction of mutations in a transcriptional regulator and a membrane protein, together with overexpression of efflux pumps, recapitulated the resistance phenotypes of the evolved strains. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance.

research.abstract: Abstract Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data exhibit strong and reproducible statistical structure. This has motivated the development of large-scale foundation models, such as TranscriptFormer, that use transformer-based architectures to learn a generative model for gene expression by embedding genes into a latent vector space. These embeddings have been used to obtain state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on downstream tasks such as cell-type classification, disease-state prediction, and cross-species learning. Here, we ask whether similar performance can be achieved without utilizing computationally intensive deep learning-based representations. Using simple, interpretable pipelines that rely on careful normalization and linear methods, we obtain SOTA or near SOTA performance across multiple benchmarks commonly used to evaluate single-cell foundation models, including outperforming foundation models on out-of-distribution tasks involving novel cell types and organisms absent from the training data. Our findings highlight the need for rigorous benchmarking and suggest that the biology of cell identity can be captured by simple linear representations of single cell gene expression data.

research.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is common, heritable (h2 ~50%) and polygenic, but the contribution of rare structural variation is largely unexamined. Using short-read whole-genome sequencing (srWGS) data from the All of Us Research Program, we tested the association of rare copy number variants (rCNV; minor allele frequency <1%) with AUD in 56,062 participants (5,410 cases, 50,652 controls) defined from electronic health records. Analyses were conducted within European-like (EUR; N=29,392), African-like (AFR; N=8,269) and Admixed American-like (AMR; N=8,049) samples and combined by cross-ancestry meta-analysis. We tested genome-wide rCNV burden, burden within AUD-related, mouse behavioral and neuropsychiatric gene sets, and individual rCNV regions. No genome-wide burden metric or individual rCNV region [≥]10 kb was associated with AUD after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Significant gene-set results were almost exclusively duplications associated with reduced AUD risk across biologically unrelated sets, suggesting a global duplication dosage effect rather than pathway-specific enrichment. In contrast, deletion count within a Neurof_UnionStringent gene set was associated with increased AUD risk (OR=1.04, FDR=0.044), and deletions in xenobiotic-response genes showed nominal associations in multiple ancestry groups. Among rCNV of all sizes, a 58 bp deletion at 16p12.1, a dosage-sensitive neuropsychiatric locus, was significant in the cross-ancestry analysis (OR=2.93, FDR=0.030) without significant heterogeneity. rCNV detectable by srWGS do not appear to contribute substantially to AUD liability at current sample sizes.

research.abstract: Although rare non-coding variants are likely involved in psychiatric disorder susceptibility, their contribution is poorly understood. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression, and targets in the brain include genes involved in neuronal development and synaptic plasticity. Because single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) can alter miRNA processing and target specificity, this can have disproportionate downstream impact on multiple genes affecting pathways that regulate biological processes, making them compelling candidates for mediating psychiatric disorder risk. We investigated rare miRNA variants in whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 25 pedigrees with diagnoses including schizophrenia, psychosis, bipolar disorder, depression, OCD, and substance use disorder. Evidence of segregation with schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders was identified for five rare miRNA variants (two seed-region, one mature-region, and two precursor-region variants), including a SNV in the mature-region of miR-4794, segregating strongly in two unrelated pedigrees and identified in a parent-offspring pair with schizophrenia from a third pedigree. One of these two pedigrees also segregates a seed-region SNV in miR-4423-3p, predicted to significantly impact expression-regulation, causing the loss of synaptic gene-targets associated with psychiatric disorders. Collectively, targets of three of the miRNAs are enriched for schizophrenia rare variant risk genes (p-value: 0.00027): six SCHEMA genes were targeted by miR-96 and four genes by miR-4423-3p. While further understanding of miRNA function and validation is required, this study demonstrates the value of integrating structural modelling, target-shift prediction, and pathway enrichment to interpret non-coding variants. This highlights the utility of WGS for identifying and investigating rare non-coding variation in psychiatric disorder susceptibility, supplementing exome-based approaches.

research.abstract: Abstract Eliminating lifelong immunosuppression can make islet transplantation a durable alternative to insulin therapy for type 1 diabetes. As short-course tolerogenic regimens are developed to replace lifelong immunosuppression, it is critical to test their robustness against perturbations such as hospital-acquired infections, which transplant recipients routinely encounter. Herein, we investigated whether rapamycin-loaded polymersomes (rPS), a subcutaneous nanotherapy that induces long-term murine islet allograft survival, can preserve host defenses in a Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin infection, and whether the resulting immune response from this distal infection relative to graft location erodes rPS-induced tolerance. rPS maintained neutrophil antibacterial activity despite inhibiting oxidative mechanisms in vitro , and rPS-treated mice demonstrated normal recovery following MRSA challenge. However, MRSA skin infection caused a decline of ∼43% in recipient survival for rPS-treated mice, despite surviving recipients retaining glucose-stimulated insulin responsiveness. This erosion of allograft acceptance coincided with a burst of IL-6 within 24h of the infection followed by elevated TNF-□ and neutrophilia at 13 days post-infection. Combining rPS with a single dose of methylprednisolone reduced IL-6 and TNF-α without altering neutrophilia, nearly doubling survival among infected recipients to 80%. Our findings demonstrate that partial dampening of inflammatory insults can restore superior islet allograft acceptance following perioperative infection.

research.abstract: Most breast cancer (BC) risk loci identified by genome wide association studies lie in noncoding regions, and traditional transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) often prioritize multiple correlated genes per locus. We applied two gene fine-mapping methods, TGVIS and M cTWAS, which jointly model gene expression, splicing and alternative polyadenylation (APA) with direct variant effects, to overall BC, estrogen receptor-negative (ER negative) BC and triple-negative BC (TNBC) in women of European and African ancestry. Using 11 BC-relevant GTEx v10 tissues, we prioritized 31, 13 and 5 candidate causal genes, respectively, in European-ancestry populations. Compared with marginal TWAS, fine-mapping reduced the number of candidate genes per locus by 72 to 88%, and credible sets explained 97 to 100% of significant marginal associations. Seven candidates were not reported by previous GTEx v8-based TWAS, including RIN3, supported only by APA, and NPAT for TNBC. Analyses across 48 tissues and brain cell types revealed brain contributions, including ARHGEF5 in oligodendrocytes. In African-ancestry populations, EN1 was prioritized for ER negative BC and TNBC through variants common in African but rare in European ancestry. These results refine BC susceptibility genes, highlight regulatory mechanisms beyond breast tissue and gene expression, and reveal the challenge of mapping GWAS variants to causal genes with currently available data.

research.abstract: Time-restricted eating (TRE) is a promising strategy to improve weight management and metabolic health, but its efficacy may vary depending on the coherence between the eating window and individual chronotype. In a randomized 12-week intervention of morning chronotype adults with overweight or obesity, early TRE (06:00h-14:00h) led to greater reductions in body fat mass compared to late TRE (12:00h-20:00h) and active control (three meals per day). Continuous glucose monitoring revealed enhanced circadian glucose rhythmicity and increased glycemic variability in early TRE, whereas postprandial glucose excursions were attenuated in late TRE. Early TRE induced the most pronounced systemic multi-omic changes, characterized by distinct transcriptional and metabolic programs, including reduced triglyceride and increased sphingomyelin levels. We found that in morning chronotype, early TRE and late TRE elicit distinct adaptations in body composition, glucose and lipid metabolism, and altered transcriptional and metabolic signatures. ClinicalTrials.gov registration no. NCT04618133 .

research.abstract: Abstract Dengue viruses 1-4 (DENV1-4) mostly circulate in endemic cycles involving humans and Aedes mosquitoes. However, rare dengue outbreaks originate from non-human primates. These spillovers are caused by sylvatic virus genotypes that are closely related to endemic strains of the same serotype, but some are caused by strains that fall between the four canonical serotypes on phylogenetic trees. It is not clear whether these genotypic differences are reflected in corresponding antigenic differences. Here, we characterized the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent strain most closely related to DENV2. On an antigenic map, QML-22 clustered with other globally representative DENV2 strains. QML-22 was not as well neutralized by antisera raised against endemic DENV2 and was better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections than other strains of DENV2. QML-22 had a cluster of distinct amino acid residues in domain I of the envelope (E) protein, with only scattered point mutations elsewhere in the envelope. A potently neutralizing anti-DENV2 antibody that targets this site in domain I of the E protein, 3F9, had >1000-fold lower neutralization of QML-22 than other endemic DENV2 strains, whereas other cross-reactive and DENV2-specific antibodies neutralized QML-22 and endemic strains to similar titers. When antisera from non-human primates infected with QML-22 or DENV2 reference strain S16803 were depleted with the heterologous virions, homologous neutralization was unaffected but heterologous neutralization was reduced, suggesting homologous neutralization was due to distinct epitopes. Evolutionary analyses showed the 3F9 epitope was under relaxed selection pressure compared to other neutralizing epitopes and that QML-22 had unique amino acids in this epitope relative to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2. These findings provide insight into the antigenic diversification of DENV and the possible evolution of new serotypes. Author summary Dengue viruses that are most distantly related to the four canonical serotypes originated in Borneo, suggesting this island is a possible site of early dengue virus diversification as well as continued evolution within an unidentified host species. Here, we find divergent strain QML-22 from Borneo shares many neutralizing epitopes with DENV2 but has a distinct epitope in an important region affecting potent DENV2 neutralization. This region of the virus also is variable within DENV2 and in other DENV serotypes, highlighting an important site of dengue virus diversification and evolution. The spillover threat of viruses like QML-22 remains unknown, but ecological changes in Borneo may increase this risk.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Circulating fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises dramatically in chronic kidney disease, particularly in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). At high concentrations, and with declining Klotho, FGF23 has been linked to renal inflammation. The cell types and transcriptional programs mediating these off-target actions remain undefined. We asked whether the diseased kidney responds to FGF23 differently from the healthy kidney, and whether any disease-specific response could be targeted. Methods Male and female DBA/2J mice received streptozotocin or vehicle to induce DKD. On day 56, mice received a single dose intravenous injection of FGF23 (0.3 µg) or vehicle, with tissue collected 1 h later for single-nucleus RNA sequencing, differential expression and regulon (inferred transcription factor activity) analysis. Candidate pathways were tested in precision-cut kidney slices using the CEBPB inhibitor ST-101. Results Streptozotocin-treated male mice developed early DKD with a 6-fold increase in urinary albumin/creatinine ratio and 50% higher blood urea nitrogen with preserved glomerular filtration rate. All major renal cell types were annotated. Canonical FGF23 signaling was intact in disease, with segment-specific target induction conserved in both conditions (e.g. Cyp24a1 in PT-S1 and DCT1). Superimposed on this were disease-restricted responses, including Wsb1 in DCT1 and Pdk4 in PT-S2, PST, DCT1 and DCT2. Regulon analysis revealed DKD-specific induction of CEBPB regulon activity by FGF23 across all analyzed tubular segments, and of STAT1 in several segments. Pre-treatment with a CEBPB inhibitor suppressed CEBPB activity, downstream NF-κB and pro-inflammatory gene sets, and immune-like cell abundance in diseased slices. Conclusion In the diabetic kidney, FGF23 engages a STAT1-CEBPB-NF-κB axis absent from healthy kidney and extending beyond its canonical Klotho-dependent target segments, identifying CEBPB as a potential treatment target for FGF23’s pathological inflammatory actions.

research.abstract: Climatic variation across latitude shapes lineage diversification and niche evolution. We integrated multilocus and genome-wide SNPs, morphological characters, historical biogeography, and phylogenetic comparative analyses for 391 sampled individuals representing 21 recognised Rana species across the Palearctic. Time-calibrated total-evidence analyses resolved three major stem lineages originating in the Early Miocene, 22.00 Mya, followed by radiations across East Asia and the central Palearctic. Biogeographic reconstruction supported a northward expansion of the Rana amurensis lineage into Siberia, c. 7.67 Mya, coinciding with relatively warm Arctic conditions. Climate-latitude relationships were weak across Ranidae, but stronger and lineage-dependent in Eastern Palearctic Rana, particularly in relation to monsoon-related climatic variables. Across lineages, broad latitudinal ranges evolved independently in Eurasian Pelophylax ridibundus, R. amurensis, R. dybowskii, and R. temporaria (c. 30.00 Mya), with additional origins in Nearctic Lithobates catesbeianus and L. sylvaticus (c. 12.00 Mya). This homoplasy highlights the influence of climatic transitions on ranid diversification.

research.abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading infectious cause of death, with drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) challenging disease control. Brazil has a high TB burden, and Rio Grande do Sul state reports persistently high incidence and drug-resistance rates. The drivers shaping the regional DR-TB burden remain poorly characterised. Methods We conducted genomic surveillance of confirmed DR-TB cases in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from January 2023 to September 2024. Clinical isolates underwent genotypic (gDST) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We analyzed 33 newly sequenced genomes and 267 historical Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes collected in 2011-2019 to characterize resistance, transmission, and spatiotemporal patterns and estimate the contributions of transmitted and acquired rifampicin resistance. Findings Molecular testing detected rifampicin resistance missed by pDST, including borderline rpoB mutations in 18.2% and emerging resistance-associated variants in 3% of the 33 analyzed isolates. Conversely, pDST detected baseline bedaquiline resistance missed by WGS in one newly diagnosed case. Among 300 genomes, 181 (60.3%) clustered into 32 genomic clusters at a 5-SNP threshold, including 12 with long-term circulation and several spanning prisons and communities. Sublineage frequencies remained stable over time, whereas we observed marked geographic structuring and localized clonal expansion. Among 178 rifampicin-resistant isolates, transmission accounted for an estimated 79.2-88.2% of resistance, corresponding to 11.8-20.8% of cases arising through de novo acquisition during treatment. Interpretation Our findings identify active transmission as the main driver of rifampicin-resistant TB in Rio Grande do Sul, with long-term transmission chains extending across both incarcerated and community settings. These results underscore the urgent need to strengthen timely TB case detection and resistance testing, enhance contact investigations, and implement targeted interventions aiming to interrupt persistent transmission chains.

research.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first–line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross–sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fisher’s exact test. Results: Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30–40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood–stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. Conclusion: These findings validate Ghana National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) guidelines emphasizing the reliability of mucopurulent specimen collection, but challenges the routine rejection of blood–stained sputum. The rising trend of indeterminate rifampicin results requires further investigation of circulating rpoB mutation profiles and quality assurance measures. Patients with indeterminate results should be further assessed using drug susceptibility testing to rule out rifampicin resistance. The findings provide actionable evidence to refine diagnostic algorithms and improve TB care in Ghana.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

research.abstract: Abstract Secondary (promiscuous) activities provide enzymes with a reservoir of latent catalytic functions, which can be leveraged during selective pressure. Here we retrace the re-emergence of glycolysis from the promiscuous activity of 1-phosphofructokinase (FruK). We evolved a hexose-degradation-deficient Escherichia coli strain on glucose and recovered non-synonymous mutations in fruK . Reverse engineering, gene deletions and transcript quantification identified a modified and strongly overexpressed fruK as the determinant of the growth phenotype. Purified FruK variants phosphorylated fructose-6-phosphate in vitro , the best variant with ∼170-fold improved catalytic efficiency over the wildtype enzyme. Crystal structures at up to 1.4 Å resolution captured FruK with ADP and either F1P, F6P or FBP bound. They identify a single active-site lysine that excludes the alternative substrate, and which E. coli FruK retains despite forgoing a 26 % gain in efficiency on its own native reaction. Since F1P, the product of the reverse reaction of FruK, is the effector of the global regulator Cra, we propose that this residue keeps glycolytic flux separate from transcriptional control. The same active-site motifs occur naturally across FruK clades, and a hexose-degradation-deficient Corynebacterium glutamicum strain converged on the same adaptation, indicating a common strategy across the Gram divide. The committed step of EMP glycolysis therefore lies a single substitution away within a widespread sugar kinase family, where it appears to be actively suppressed.

items.title: Introgressive hybridization as a potential source of evolutionary rescue in an extreme peripheral environment
items.summary: Range-margin populations often experience demographic and environmental conditions that constrain their adaptive potential. Genetic drift can erode diversity, while gene flow from the range core may swamp locally favoured alleles. These limitations may be severe in extreme environments, yet how peripheral populations persist and adapt there remains poorly understood. Introgression from…

research.abstract: Abstract Range-margin populations often experience demographic and environmental conditions that constrain their adaptive potential. Genetic drift can erode diversity, while gene flow from the range core may swamp locally favoured alleles. These limitations may be severe in extreme environments, yet how peripheral populations persist and adapt there remains poorly understood. Introgression from neighbouring lineages may address both constraints by adding genetic variation and introducing alleles pre-tested by selection, potentially contributing to evolutionary rescue. Here, we analyse 112 whole genomes across the great tit ( Parus major ) complex to investigate how peripheral populations persist and adapt, focusing on P. m. intermedius , a grey-plumaged population in arid northeastern Iran at the southeastern margin of the yellow-breasted major lineage, bordering the grey bokharensis lineage. We found that intermedius falls within major in the first nuclear species tree of the complex and the mitochondrial phylogeny. As expected for a peripheral population, it is genetically differentiated, yet retains relatively high nucleotide diversity and carries low-level genomewide bokharensis ancestry. Against low genome-wide differentiation from major , a 35-kb region on chromosome 24 shows excess allele sharing with bokharensis up to six-fold above the genome-wide average, a bokharensis origin in local genealogies and ancestry inference, and reduced diversity and negative Tajima’s D consistent with positive selection. This region contains BCO2 , a carotenoid-cleaving gene, with differentiated 5 ′ untranslated-region variants, implicating regulatory variation in carotenoid-based plumage. Our findings suggest that introgression from closely related lineages can buffer peripheral populations against loss of genetic variation and facilitate adaptation to harsh, divergent habitats beyond the range core, highlighting hybridization as an underappreciated source of resilience at species’ range limits. Significance Statement Adaptation often fails at range margins, where populations are expected to be differentiated yet genetically depleted, and gene flow from the core can swamp locally favoured alleles. Introgression could counter both, buffering by adding variation and enabling adaptation through pre-tested alleles. We examined these roles in Parus major intermedius , a peripheral great tit population in the putative contact zone between the yellow Eurasian major and grey bokharensis lineages. We analysed 112 genomes from across Eurasia; the first nuclear species tree places intermedius within major . Intermedius is differentiated yet retains most of its diversity and carries low-level bokharensis ancestry, while one region stands out: containing the carotenoid-cleaving gene BCO2 , it retains bokharensis ancestry far above genome-wide levels, consistent with selection. More broadly, hybridization with neighbouring lineages may be an overlooked source of variation and adaptive potential for range-margin populations facing extreme or changing environments.

research.abstract: Abstract Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) poses a major threat to the global swine industry. Although coronavirus discontinuous transcription is well characterized, the classical model cannot fully explain the diversity of viral RNA junctions, while conventional genome annotations may underestimate viral protein-coding capacity. To address these gaps, we integrated time-resolved RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), cycloheximide (CHX)- and harringtonine (HAR)-treated ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), comparative genomics, and peptide mass spectrometry to investigate PEDV RNA expression and hidden coding potential. RNA-seq revealed that, at 3 hours post-infection (hpi), the 3’ genomic region exhibited strong relative coverage enrichment, whereas the relative contribution of the 5’ replicase-coding region increased rapidly between 3 and 5 hpi, suggesting a possible transition from sgRNA-dominated RNA accumulation toward enhanced genomic RNA replication. Genome-wide junction analysis identified 43,635 distinct noncanonical RNA junctions, although canonical sgRNA junctions accounted for 95.5% of all junction-supporting reads. Several abundant noncanonical sgRNAs were predicted to generate novel coding products, including N-x4, N-x2, M-x3, and M-x2, short peptides encoded within the 3’ untranslated region (UTR), and two distinct N-terminally truncated S proteins, thereby expanding the potential coding repertoire of PEDV. Genome-wide reading-frame analysis uncovered a pronounced asymmetry in hidden coding potential, identifying 68 overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) longer than 40 amino acids in the +1 reading frame, compared with only three in the +2 frame. Ribo-seq further revealed a progressive redistribution of viral ribosome occupancy toward structural protein-coding regions during the later stages of infection. By integrating HAR-associated translation initiation-site enrichment with CHX-based ORF-level translation analysis, we identified several noncanonical ORFs with strong translation-associated evidence, including N-x1, N-x2, S-x1, and ORF1b-x13. Moreover, peptide mass spectrometry detected a characteristic peptide corresponding to N-x1 in infected samples, providing independent proteomic evidence for the expression of this previously unannotated viral protein. Together, these findings uncover extensive noncanonical RNA synthesis and hidden protein-coding capacity in PEDV, establishing a foundation for understanding novel viral gene expression strategies and their potential evolutionary and pathogenic significance.

research.abstract: Abstract Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree. A GenomegaMap scan identified 163 of 3,147 genes with ω₀ > 1. These genes were depleted among core genes and enriched among cloud genes, a pattern consistent with positive selection on recently acquired genes but also with the retention of slightly deleterious variation in young genes. A putative IS transposase (K07497) was the most consistent functional enrichment signal, which led us to analyze insertion sequence (IS) elements directly. In group 12, complete IS copies within genomes were more often near-identical than in other groups (OR = 1.46), consistent with more recent IS activity, and genes with ω₀ > 1 were 2.9 times more likely than other accessory genes to lie within 5 kb of an IS element (8.8% vs. 3.0%; permutation p = 0.0006) after excluding IS-encoded genes. We did not detect this association in any other group, and most genes under selection were not IS-proximal.
